subject: Quantitative Aptitude
topic: Work and Time — Efficiency Problems (W11 B2)

questions.stem: A can complete a work in 10 days, B in 15 days. In how many days will they finish it together?
questions.explanation: B is correct. A's rate = 1/10 per day; B's rate = 1/15 per day. Combined = 1/10+1/15 = 3/30+2/30 = 5/30 = 1/6. Together they finish in 6 days. Verify: In 6 days, A does 6/10=3/5; B does 6/15=2/5; total=3/5+2/5=1 ✓. Trap: 5 = 10+15)/2×(product)/(sum) error; 12 = harmonic confusion.

questions.stem: A alone can do a piece of work in 12 days. A and B together can do it in 8 days. In how many days can B alone do the work?
questions.explanation: B is correct. B's rate = (A+B) rate - A rate = 1/8-1/12 = 3/24-2/24 = 1/24. B alone takes 24 days. Verify: A+B in 8 days: A does 8/12=2/3; B does 8/24=1/3; total=1 ✓. Trap: 20 = 12+8=20 (wrong — just adds the days); 16 = 2×8 (wrong).

questions.stem: A, B, and C together can complete a task in 4 days. A alone takes 8 days and B alone takes 12 days. How many days does C alone need?
A can do a piece of work in 15 days. A and B together can do it in 10 days. B and C together can do it in 20 days. How long will C alone take?
If 8 workers complete a job in 12 days working 6 hours a day, how many workers are needed to complete the same job in 8 days working 9 hours a day?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Total work = 8 workers × 12 days × 6 hours = 576 worker-hours. New scenario: 8 days × 9 hours = 72 hours per worker. Workers needed = 576/72 = 8 workers. Verify: 8×8×9 = 576 worker-hours ✓. Trap: 6 = 576/(8×12) = 6 (divides by only two factors, wrong); 9 = uses wrong calculation.

questions.stem: A is twice as efficient as B. Together they complete a task in 12 days. How many days does A alone need?
questions.explanation: B is correct. A is twice as efficient → if B takes x days, A takes x/2 days. Combined rate: 1/(x/2)+1/x = 2/x+1/x = 3/x = 1/12. x = 36 days (B), x/2 = 18 days (A). Verify: A's rate=1/18; B's rate=1/36; combined=2/36+1/36=3/36=1/12. Together=12 days ✓. Trap: 24 = uses B's days ÷ 2 = 36/2 but mistakenly computes 12×2=24; 16 = wrong formula.

questions.stem: A, B, and C can complete a work in 12, 15, and 20 days respectively. All three start together. After 2 days, C leaves. How many more days will A and B take to finish the remaining work?
questions.explanation: C is correct. LCM(12,15,20)=60. A=5 units/day; B=4 units/day; C=3 units/day. Together=12 units/day. In 2 days: 24 units done. Total work=60. Remaining=36 units. (A+B) rate=9 units/day. Time=36÷9=4 days. Verify: 2 days at 12/day=24 done; 4 days at 9/day=36 more; 24+36=60=total ✓. Trap: 3 = 36÷12 (divides by combined rate instead of A+B rate); 2 = 18÷9 (halves remaining incorrectly).

questions.stem: A can complete a job in 9 days. B can complete it in 18 days. A works alone for 3 days, then B joins. How many more days do they need together to finish the job?
questions.explanation: B is correct. A's rate = 1/9. Work done by A in 3 days = 3/9 = 1/3. Remaining = 1-1/3 = 2/3. (A+B) rate = 1/9+1/18 = 2/18+1/18 = 3/18 = 1/6. Time for remaining 2/3 = (2/3)/(1/6) = (2/3)×6 = 4 days. Verify: Together in 4 days: A does 4/9+B does 4/18=8/18+4/18=12/18=2/3; total=1/3+2/3=1 ✓. Trap: 3 = assumes B does the same as A; 6 = time for B alone to do remaining 2/3 (=2/3×18=12 days, not 6).

questions.stem: 18 men can complete a piece of work in 10 days. After 4 days, 6 men leave. How many more days are needed to complete the remaining work?
questions.explanation: C is correct. Total work = 18×10 = 180 man-days. Work done in 4 days = 18×4 = 72 man-days. Remaining = 180-72 = 108 man-days. After 6 men leave: 12 men remain. Days = 108÷12 = 9 days. Verify: 12×9 = 108 ✓. Total = 72+108 = 180 ✓. Trap: 8 = 96÷12 (wrong — computes remaining as 96); 7 = 84÷12 (wrong remaining).

questions.stem: P, Q, and R together complete a work in 4 days. P and Q together can do it in 6 days. In how many days can R alone do the work?
questions.explanation: C is correct. R's rate = (P+Q+R) rate - (P+Q) rate = 1/4-1/6 = 3/12-2/12 = 1/12. R alone takes 12 days. Verify: (P+Q+R) in 4 days at 1/4 per day; (P+Q) at 1/6 per day; R at 1/12 per day; 1/6+1/12=2/12+1/12=3/12=1/4 ✓. Trap: 8 = 4+6-2 (wrong arithmetic); 10 = common distractor.
